message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the clade that includes the orders **Carnivora** (lion) and **Perissodactyla** (zebra).  
That ancestor is the last common ancestor of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which also contains the orders Cetartiodactyla (even‑toed ungulates), Chiroptera (bats), and Eulipotyphla (hedgehogs, moles, etc.).  

In other words, the most recent common ancestor of lion and zebra is the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria, which lived roughly 70 million years ago.
